category_title: High-achieving students who dominate group work and exclude peers in competitive settings
scenario_title: Mixed-ability group work on multiple-choice assessment
minimal_context: The student is working in a mixed-ability group on a multiple-choice assessment with the goal of achieving high scores on the group test.

dialogue.speaker: tutor
dialogue.message: Please continue working with your mixed-ability group on this multiple-choice assessment to achieve high scores on your group test.

dialogue.speaker: student
dialogue.message: I've already gone through the first section and I'm just giving them the answers so we can go faster. I don't want to be held back by my slower teammates.

dialogue.speaker: tutor
dialogue.message: What do you think about discussing the questions with the rest of the group?

dialogue.speaker: student
dialogue.message: I always appreciate contribution of all members. However, I have to say I feel safer if the contribution comes from a good student. Whenever we receive products from a less able member, we need to spend time rechecking so it takes our time. When they get stuck, I just jump into their mouth to keep us moving.

dialogue.speaker: tutor
dialogue.message: The instructions ask that the group works together to choose the answers.

dialogue.speaker: student
dialogue.message: It's a multiple-choice assessment, and I know that eventually I'm the one who makes the final decisions in choosing the right answers for the group anyway. There's really no need to listen to others; we can just go ahead with using my own answers.

task.content: working on an assessment as a multiple-choice test
task.learning_goal: achieve high scores on both individual and group tests

context.materials: multiple-choice question test, group project, powerpoint presentation
context.social_setting: mixed-ability groups that consisted of a balance of five low- to five high-achievers

challenging_behavior_trigger.condition: when dealing with a multiple-choice assessment
challenging_behavior_trigger.observable_behavior: decided that there was no need to listen to others and that they could go ahead with using their own answers
challenging_behavior_trigger.internal_state: might know that eventually they were the ones who made the final decisions in choosing the right answers for the group

behavior_patterns.observable_behavior: usually ‘jumped into their mouth ’(i.e., demeaned them)
behavior_patterns.internal_state: not excited about participating in cooperative learning groups because they had to help, monitor and explain material
